notes:
Summary: Seabright is a cloud-first contact center platform serving two multiregional customers (retail + telecom). Primary push: reduce agent friction during seasonal spikes and avoid SLA breaches when incident bursts occur. They want an architecture that degrades gracefully (fallbacks, throttles, model variants) rather than full outage.

Initial requirements (from discovery call 2024-10-18):
- Workloads: realtime agent assist (latency critical, 75th pctl < 120ms preferred for token streaming), asynchronous ticket summarization (batch nightly), and automated tool-calling for order lookups.
- Throughput: baseline 8k concurrent agent sessions across EU/NA, seasonal peaks up to 30k+ concurrent during Black Friday-like events.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; willing to pay for reserved predictable capacity if we can demonstrate unit cost reduction vs cloud GPUs.
- Model preferences: open-weight models (Llama/Redwood-verified) on quantized variants for production; fallback to smaller family models during overload.
- Reliability: need automated routing by region + capacity tier + model-compatibility fallback. Must avoid cascading failures when queues backpressure.
- Security: SSO (SAML), full audit logs, KMS integration, and EU data residency for some customers. SOC2 in scope.

Recent interactions / timeline:
- 2024-10-05: Lead (VP Eng) inbound via whitepaper download. Jordan assigned.
- 2024-10-18: Discovery call (Fireflies ff-20241018-17-seabright-demo). Collected latency profile and traffic shape.
- 2024-11-02: Technical deep-dive with platform infra (Maya + Seabright infra). Discussed KV caching, autoscale thresholds.
- 2024-11-16: Sec & compliance call. Customer requested SOC2 attestation + KMS key escrow architecture.
- 2024-12-07: Pilot kickoff meeting; scheduled 2-week spike sim. (Fireflies ff-20241207-03-spike-sim).
- 2024-12-14: Pilot config draft shared (Drive link). SE created INF-4127 for runtime kernel timing question.

Pilot scope / POC plan (short):
- 2-week Dedicated cluster provisioned in NA and EU; ingest a trimmed subset of production traffic.
- Run synthetic surge scenarios that mimic hour-long 4x and 8x peaks. Measure 95th/99th latency, token cost, and fallback behavior.
- Validate automatic routing + KV cache hit improvements for repeated customer contexts.
- Run canary rollouts with model variant fallback policies.

Customer quotes / voice of customer:
- "We don't need perfect answers when the office is on fire; we need predictable behavior and clear fallbacks." — Head of Ops
- "If you can show cost per handled contact drops during peaks and SLAs hold, procurement will greenlight." — VP Finance

Open technical questions (from SE):
- How does Redwood's autoscaler behave under sustained 8x bursts? Need precise scaling latency numbers.
- Can we schedule guaranteed reserved burst nodes for specific peak windows?
- Backpressure semantics: preferred mechanism is queued TTL + graceful degrade to short-context models.

Next steps (action items):
- Maya to deliver Dedicated pilot config and estimated cost by 2024-12-22.
- Security to provide SOC2 + KMS integration note (Jordan to forward to Seabright sec team).
- Run first small-scale surge test 2024-12-28 (non-prod) — measure autoscale time and tail latency.

- SLO: 95th token latency < 250ms during 4x surge, < 400ms acceptable for 8x with fallback.
- Cost: <= 30% increase in ops spend during peaks vs baseline (with target of per-contact cost reduction long term).
- Ops: automatic rollback + canary for model updates; audit logs enabled.
